dedupe_keys.name: bass2000 solar survey archive paris observatory

description: BASS2000 is the French solar survey archive at the Paris Observatory and a regular member of the World Data Centre for Solar Activity. Its home page shows the latest observations from the Meteospace and Climso instruments at Pic du Midi, the Nançay decametric array (full-resolution dynamic spectra with polarisation, in PNG and RT1 files), the Meudon spectroheliograph and the USET station of the Royal Observatory of Belgium, with a date search for any day. Menus lead to latest movies, the solar spectrum, live Sun webcams, queries for observations, specific content, solar features and synoptic maps, the Heliophysics Feature Catalogue, ephemerides, the SOLAP solar explorer, the collection before 1980, the THEMIS archive and the archive of the Meudon solar tower, plus guides, instruments, software and a data availability page. Access is free and online; no licence is stated on the home page. Caveats: the archive is aimed at solar physics, so users need to derive space weather indicators themselves, and the home page gives no terms. Coverage is global solar observation from French and Belgian instruments, with historical collections before 1980. It supports space weather hazard analysis for power grids, satellites and radio communications, such as reconstructing solar flares and radio bursts behind past disruptions; related records are the OFRAME space weather dashboard and the Spanish space weather service SeNMEs.
